name: Pop-Art Comic
summary: A printed 1960s comic book come alive: brush-ink outlines, flat process colours, Ben-Day dots and slipped colour plates.
description: Every sprite looks like it was printed on cheap newsprint: thick black brush outlines that get heavier on the shadow side, flat CMYK-ish process colours, halftone dot crescents instead of gradients, a solid spot-black rim on the shadow edge and a cyan or magenta colour plate that is slightly out of register. The ground is warm newsprint where every region gets its own rotated dot screen, separated by inked contour lines. Kills explode into jagged yellow bursts with POW!/ZONK! balloons in Bangers.
avoidFor: calm cozy sims that need soft lighting
games needing many dark night scenes

difficulty.why: Ink outline, halftone dots and colour-plate offset have to be applied to every new object individually; the ground is already expensive.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screenPx/360 × 1.4), 3, 5) pixels per world unit and drawn scaled; ground is computed per pixel at up to 2.5 px/unit in 256-unit chunks.
technique.summary: A 'part painter' builds each sprite from simple shapes: clip -> flat process colour -> optional Ben-Day dot overlay -> halftone shade crescent (shape minus shape shifted toward the light) -> solid black spot crescent -> details -> white shine ellipses -> double brush stroke outline. Afterwards a cyan or magenta silhouette is drawn behind the sprite offset by 0.5 units (misregistered plate).
technique.linework: Ink #1b1620, 1.0 world unit default (0.6–1.45 depending on part size; head 1.15, brute body 1.45), round caps and joins. Each outline is stroked twice: once at width w, once at 0.85 w shifted (+0.3 w, +0.36 w) so the stroke is heavier at bottom-right. Interior ink lines (folds, mouths, cracks) are 0.4–0.6 units. Ground contours are 0.84–2.08 units wide, varying with noise like a brush.
technique.shading: No gradients. Shade = a dot screen in a darker sister colour (dot radius factor 0.45–0.62) inside a crescent on the shadow side; a smaller solid-black crescent hugs the very edge. Light comes from top-left, so crescents use negative offsets (e.g. [-2.3, -1.9]) and sit at the bottom-right. Some parts get a light Ben-Day overlay (rf 0.3–0.42) of a complementary colour over the flat fill.
technique.lighting: Top-left key light only, expressed by shade crescents and white shine ellipses at top-left. Glows are not blurred: a lantern/hero light is a hex grid of yellow dots whose radius falls off as (1-d)^0.7. Shadows are two concentric ellipses of ink dots. Screen corners get a vignette of big ink dots.
technique.texture: Newsprint paper with per-pixel grain (±2.3 % hash noise plus faint fibres), slight large-scale yellowing (±4 %), rotated anti-aliased dot screens whose dot size follows a tone noise field.

paletteRules: Every colour has a darker 'dot' sister used only as halftone dots for shading (orange #ff8a1c -> #e0301e, cape #2c6ad0 -> #0f2f80). Never shade by darkening the fill itself.
Black is always the warm ink #1b1620, never #000. Outlines, spot blacks and shadow dots share it.
Ground regions are pale (paper tint) with mid-saturation dots; actors are fully saturated process colours so they pop off the floor.
Misregistered plates are only cyan #2ec4ef or magenta #e0338f (props use pink #ff3d6e at 45 %), drawn behind the sprite at 60–70 % alpha.
Complementary dot overlays are encouraged (cyan dots on magenta, magenta on violet, yellow on magenta).
No gradients, no blur, no soft glows anywhere; tone is always dot size or dot density.

typography.role: Onomatopoeia (POW!, ZONK!), damage numbers, HUD numbers, titles, card names
typography.css: font: 400 38px/1 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1620; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #e8262c;

typography.role: Body text, labels, card descriptions, hints (often uppercase)
typography.css: font: 700 16px/1.25 'Comic Neue', 'Comic Sans MS', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #1b1620;

background.summary: Warm newsprint split into large organic regions (meadow, autumn field, night, graveyard, paths). Each region has its own paper tint and its own rotated dot screen (angle 15°–60°, spacing 2.8–3.3 units, dot radius 15–36 % of spacing modulated by a tone noise). Regions are separated by brush-ink contours, paths get diagonal speed hatching along their edges, and small ink decals (grass tufts, flowers, cracks, splats) are scattered on top.
layers: Paper tint per region × large-scale yellowing (±4 %)
Rotated anti-aliased dot screen per region, multiply-blended, radius from tone noise
Ink contour lines between regions (half-width 0.42–1.04 units) + diagonal hatching on path edges
Ink decals: 3-blade grass tufts, 5-petal flowers, leaves, cracks, stones, rare ink splats
Halftone-dot contact shadows and yellow dot glow under the hero
Props (trees, fences, gravestones, pumpkins) baked with the same part painter + pink plate
Screen overlay: corner vignette of ink dots, paper gutter and a jittered black panel frame

characters.summary: Chunky, readable cartoon figures built from 10–20 primitive parts (ellipses, capsules, polygons, superellipse pumpkins, turnip beziers). Hero ~21 × 34 units (baked at 1.12×), small enemy ~17 × 28 (0.92×), brute ~48 × 66. Parts are painted back-to-front: back leg, back arm, body, front leg, front arm, head. Faces are carved holes (black rim + yellow inside shifted down-right) or solid ink shapes with tiny white catchlights. Four walk frames (idle, contact A, passing, contact B) plus a yellow 'flash' copy of every frame, both facings.
rules: Outline everything; the outline is the silhouette. Heads/bodies get thicker outlines (1.1–1.45) than limbs (0.8–0.85).
Each part has exactly one shade crescent on the bottom-right and one thinner spot-black crescent inside it.
Two-tone bodies: top colour above a wavy ink line, bottom colour below, each with its own dot screen.
Eyes and mouths are high-contrast: yellow #ffe23a in ink, or ink shapes with cyan/white highlights.
Every actor type gets a different dominant colour and a different silhouette (round pumpkin, teardrop turnip, wavy-tailed ghost, huge brute).
A cyan plate behind solid actors, a magenta plate behind ghosts, pink behind props – this fringe sells the print look.

effects.name: Hit impact
effects.how: 8-point yellow star (r 6.5/2.4) with red Ben-Day dots and a white inner star, plus 7 black tapered speed-line wedges radiating out; enemy is overdrawn with its baked yellow flash frame at alpha = min(0.9, flash × 1.4) and squashed (sx +18 %, sy −14 %).

effects.name: Kill burst
effects.how: 12-point jagged star (r 10/5.6, jitter 0.38) filled with yellow, white or orange, two dot rings (rf 0.62 out to r 6.2, rf 0.95 inside r 3.6) in red/cyan, ink outline 0.9. Pops in with outBack in 16 % of its 0.34 s life, then slowly grows and fades the last 40 %.

effects.name: Onomatopoeia balloon
effects.how: Bangers 11 units text centered in a 13-point jagged star balloon (inner 0.72) with a darker offset plate (-0.8, +0.7, 70 %), dot rim outside 62 % of the radius, 1.0 ink outline, text with a 0.9-unit hard drop shadow, 0.2 × font-size ink stroke. Max 3 on screen, at most one every 1.3 s, 30 % chance per kill; bosses always.

effects.name: Damage number
effects.how: Bangers 9.5 units white (13 units yellow on crits) with a 0.22 × font-size ink stroke and a magenta (crit: cyan) copy offset (-0.7, +0.6). Crits sit in a white 11-point star balloon and get red halftone in the lower half of the letters.

effects.name: Chunks and ink drops
effects.how: Death throws 4–9 baked polygon chunks in the enemy's colours (with spot-black crescent) and 2–6 round ink droplets on gravity arcs; ghosts drop cyan droplets.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: Two copies of the hero tinted cyan and magenta at 60 % alpha, offset 6 and 12 units behind the dash direction, plus 4 black speed lines 16–24 units long.

effects.name: Spawn burst
effects.how: Enemies erupt from a flattened (y × 0.45) yellow 12-point star with red dots and a black hole, scaled by outBack, while their sprite grows with outElastic.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: Cream seed sprite with orange halftone shade, magenta plate, spinning via y-squash (0.6–1.0), trailed by three black triangular streaks (15/10/11 units long).

ui.summary: Hard-edged comic panels: newsprint or process-colour fills, 3 px ink borders, zero radius, solid 4–8 px offset drop shadows in ink, skewed bars (skewX −10°) filled with dotted colour, Bangers numbers with a 16-direction ink text outline, speech-bubble kill counter, starburst LEVEL UP title, slightly rotated cards with dotted colour headers.

motion: Walk: frames 1,2,3,2 (contact A, passing, contact B, passing; frame 0 = idle) at anim × 0.4 cycles; body lifts sin(f·π) × 1.8 units and tilts ±0.05 rad per step.
Idle: breathing squash sy = 1 + 0.025·sin(3.2 t), sx = 1 − 0.018·sin(3.2 t).
Small enemy: 4 frames at anim × 0.85, waddle rotation sin × 0.09 rad, hop 1.2 units, 5 % squash at ground contact.
Brute: 4 frames at anim × 0.32, contact squash (1 − up)^3 × 7 %, rotation ±0.03 rad – heavy and slow.
Ghost: 4 frames at 7 fps (tail wave), floats 4.5 units up and bobs ±1.6 at 2.6 rad/s, leans into velocity ±0.14 rad.
Pops use overshoot easing (outBack / outElastic); numbers pop 0.3 -> 1.35 -> 1.0 scale in the first 24 % of life.
Hit flash decays quickly; death = 0.2 s inflate to 1.25× in the yellow impact frame, then shrink to 0 by 0.42 s while the burst takes over.
HUD hurt shake: 0.22 s steps(3) jitter of ±4 px and ±1.5°.
do: Draw every part through one painter routine so fill, dots, shade crescent, spot black and double outline are always consistent.
Bake sprites once (both facings + a flash frame) and only blit at runtime.
Shade with dot size: bigger dots = darker; use the colour's darker sister for the dots.
Slip a cyan or magenta plate 0.5 units down-left behind every sprite.
Keep actors fully saturated and the ground pale so hordes read against the floor.
Use jagged star balloons + Bangers for every loud event, but rate-limit them (max 3 at once).
Use hard offset drop shadows (no blur) on all UI panels.
Keep the light top-left for every object, including UI icons.
dont: Don't use gradients, blur, shadowBlur or soft glows – everything is dots or flat.
Don't use pure #000 black or thin hairline outlines; ink is #1b1620 and at least 0.4 units.
Don't align dot screens of different regions at the same angle and spacing – each needs its own screen.
Don't fill the screen with onomatopoeia; more than 3 balloons turns into noise.
Don't give enemies the same dominant colour as the ground region they walk on.
Don't round UI corners or use translucent glassy panels.
Don't draw per-pixel halftone for sprites every frame – bake it.
performance: All characters (4 frames × normal/flash × 2 facings), props, bursts, chunks, shadows and glows are baked once in init at 3–5 px per unit; runtime is pure drawImage. Text sprites are cached per value (cleared above 600 entries). The hot spot is the ground: every pixel evaluates up to 4 region distances (bilinear from a 4-unit noise grid with gradient-based signed distance), 1 rotated dot screen, grain and hatching – done per 256-unit chunk as a generator that yields every 2 rows, resolution capped at 2.5 px/unit. The screen overlay is baked once per resolution and only non-empty tiles are blitted.
